evidence: Read CONTEXT.txt whole first (the "Before you begin" section, shared with S23 and S24), then DRAFT.txt, SOURCE.txt and the_change. The draft occurs once, opening the fourth paragraph, and the unchanged sentences after it ("If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can..." and the stop lines) pick up without a seam. Against the words it replaces it is nearly verbatim, with three small deltas only: "Deciding to do it." to "Decide to do it.", "Something else?" to "etc.", and the colon after "what you are going to do" to a full stop; the old "this" is kept in "How will you coax yourself to do this?", as the_change says. No step is added or dropped relative to the replaced words. Meaning: SOURCE's published lines are (1) decide what kind of encouragement is welcome and (2) preview eye closure, any repeated exit and re-entry, and the return. The draft carries (1) as the coax question with "spacious" and "warm and held", and (2) as the three preview questions (eyes; out and back in; the end, which the paragraph before has already tied to coming back). One note that is not a defect of this swap: the published third kind of encouragement, "a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling", is not named in the draft, but it is not in the words replaced either ("Something else?"), and "etc." leaves that slot open; so this change loses nothing. No claim, hedge, summary or fact is added. Reads right in place: the same jotted-prompt register as the paragraph above ("Think about what you want to do. Are there things you don't want to do today?"), "etc." sits like the "whatever" that closes the list in that paragraph, and I hear no different writer. Tell rows: three are actually happening, as one thing, and I judge them justified. T02, T09 and T13: the passage is a run of nine short, equal-weight prompts that expands the published outline and could be regenerated from it. Justified because that form is his published form and the replaced words' form (a pre-session planning list of separate decisions: how to coax, eyes, exit and re-entry, the end), the swap neither adds nor removes a step, the draft has uneven bits of its own ("etc.", the specific "come out and go back in again"), and the unchanged rest of the paragraph carries the reasons and the aside ("even if a part tells you that you do"). Looked at and judged absent: T19 ("Preview what you are going to do." is the instruction itself, the published verb, not a bare announcement, and the old colon is gone, so no T25); T22 (the section's genre, and reasons follow in the paragraph); T07 ("etc." comes from an open list, not stage business); T24 (the questions are left for the reader to answer); T26 ("will you" and "make it" are working parallels, and this/it is the section's own anaphor); T15 (form changes, not rarer synonyms); T06 ("warm and held" echoes the published "warm company"); T12 (the open list ends in etc.); the rest absent, with no first-person stake, scene, closer, tic word, kid-naming, invented fact or study claim. Linter: B7 "What will you do at the end?" is not the paragraph's end in context (the recording line and the stop lines follow); accepted. D9: a same-slot swap of Emulate's version cannot reorder anything; accepted, with T13 and T09 checked above. E23: the "Before you begin" page is where a preparation paragraph belongs, the replaced paragraph was the same, and the paragraph's later sentences give reasons; accepted. E36/E41 12.2: the questions address the reader planning his own session and the replaced words had the same density; accepted. O29 three questions: they are the reader's own preview prompts, which the text does not answer, they follow the published preview items, and the run is the replaced paragraph's; accepted. R1 "Decide to do it.": "it" is the practice, which unchanged sentences in the section name the same way ("You can do it on something you want to experience more of", "haven't done it for a while", "to do it") and the very next sentence says "do this"; the nearest competing referent is "deepen yourself" at the end of the paragraph before, but the paragraph break, the heading and the next sentence settle it; accepted ("Decide to do this." would be tighter, not required).
